context_notes: You work in Australia: the lenders, the rules and the money are Australian.

interview.about: how mortgage brokers run a loan from first enquiry to settlement

goals.learn: What takes most of a broker's time and attention in a normal week, and what they have done about it
How documents are collected from clients, and what happens when that goes wrong
Who decides what software the business pays for, and what was last bought or dropped

topics.opener: What has taken most of your attention at work over the last couple of weeks?
Walk me through the last loan where you had to collect documents from a client.
What was the last piece of software the business started or stopped paying for?

personas.name: Dana Whitlock
personas.personality: Blunt, short of time, suspicious of new software
bio: Eleven years broking, the last four on her own, from a spare room at home.
Writes four or five loans a month, mostly first home buyers sent by two local real estate agents.
Does everything herself, from the first phone call to the settlement gift, and has no assistant.
Pays for what her aggregator makes her use and very little else, and has cancelled most of what she has tried.

personas.name: Marcus Oyelaran
personas.personality: Measured, delegates the detail, watches cost
bio: Runs the firm and signs off every subscription. Writes few loans himself now.
Has two loan processors who prepare and lodge the applications his brokers bring in.
Hears about problems when a client complains or a settlement is at risk, and not before.
Changed the firm's customer system three years ago, and still hears about it from his longest-serving broker.

personas.name: Jess Tran
personas.role: Mortgage broker in a twelve-broker firm, on commission
personas.personality: Friendly and quick, dislikes paperwork, takes the firm's systems as given
bio: Three years broking, after five in a bank branch. Most of her clients are refinancing.
Uses whatever the firm provides, and does not know what any of it costs.
Hands a file to the firm's processing team once the client has signed, and chases it when it stalls.
Keeps her own list of where each client is up to, in a notebook, because she trusts it more than the system.
